subject: environmental-science
title: Erosion: Sheet, Rill, Gully
welcome_lead: How soils disappear: drop by raindrop, channel by channel.
meta_desc: A-Level Environmental Science adventure on soil erosion processes and the USLE.
final_note: Topsoil forms at ~0.1 mm yr⁻¹ but erodes 10–100× faster under poor management.

concepts.def: Uniform thin-layer removal by overland flow on gentle slopes.
Small concentrated channels (<30 cm deep) forming on tilled fields.
Large channels (>30 cm deep) that cannot be ploughed across.
Soil dislodgement by raindrop impact; initial step in erosion.
Universal Soil Loss Equation: A = R·K·LS·C·P (Wischmeier & Smith).
Vegetation planted to protect soil from erosion between cash crops.

walkthroughs.body_html: Raindrop impact, sheet flow, rill development and gully formation are sequential intensification of erosion.
A (t ha⁻¹ yr⁻¹) = R (rainfall erosivity) × K (soil erodibility) × LS (slope) × C (cover) × P (practice).
Contour ploughing, terracing, cover cropping and no-till each reduce specific USLE factors.

mcqs.q: Which USLE factor changes most with land management?

numericals.q: Using USLE A=R·K·LS·C·P with R=200, K=0.3, LS=1.5, C=0.2, P=0.5, soil loss (t ha⁻¹ yr⁻¹) is?

free_texts.q: Acronym of the soil-loss equation by Wischmeier and Smith.
